items.q: Nōnne rēx Mīnōs Thēseum persequī coepit?
items.en: Didn't King Minos begin to pursue Theseus?
items.hint: nōnne expects 'yes' (Ita / Certē); persequī is a deponent infinitive

items.q: Cūr Mīnōs Thēseum cōnsequī nōn potuit?
items.en: Why couldn't Minos catch up with Theseus?
items.hint: a quia/quod clause; the comparison is tam … quam ('as fast as')

items.q: Quis fīlum cōnfēcerat et Ariadnae dederat?
items.en: Who had made the thread and given it to Ariadne?
items.hint: the antecedent of quī; the verbs are pluperfect

items.q: Quandō Syra dē fugā Daedalī nārrābit?
items.en: When will Syra tell about Daedalus' escape?
items.hint: an adverb of time

items.q: Cūr Syra hodiē nārrāre nōn pergit?
items.en: Why doesn't Syra go on telling the story today?
items.hint: ad + the gerund (ad nārrandum = for telling) or in + the ablative gerund

items.q: Ad quid Quīntus parātus est?
items.en: For what is Quintus ready?
items.hint: the gerund in the accusative after ad

items.q: Cūr Syra reliquam fābulam Quīntō nārrābit?
items.en: Why will Syra tell Quintus the rest of the story?
items.hint: a quoniam clause; cupidus takes the gerund in the genitive (audiendī)

items.q: Quālis vir erat Daedalus?
items.en: What kind of man was Daedalus?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative describing vir

items.q: Cūr Icarus fessus est?
items.en: Why is Icarus tired?
items.hint: the gerund in the ablative (cause/means: 'from walking')

items.q: Num is quī sē ipse iuvāre nōn vult auxilium deōrum meret?
items.en: Does the man who won't help himself deserve the gods' help?
items.hint: num expects 'no'; the subject is a relative clause (quī … nōn vult)

items.q: Quid Daedalus iam excōgitāvit?
items.en: What has Daedalus already devised?
items.hint: an accusative object with a genitive attached

items.q: Quōmodo Daedalus et Icarus ē labyrinthō ēvolābunt?
items.en: How will Daedalus and Icarus fly out of the labyrinth?
items.hint: per + accusative ('through'); āera is a Greek accusative of āēr

items.q: Quid ad volandum necessārium est?
items.en: What is necessary for flying?
items.hint: the nominative subject; ad volandum is ad + gerund

items.q: Cūr Icarus et pater volāre nōn possunt?
items.en: Why can't Icarus and his father fly?
items.hint: a quoniam clause with a perfect verb and a dative receiver

items.q: Quōmodo nātūra ipsa mūtārī potest?
items.en: How can nature itself be changed?
items.hint: an ablative of means ('by my skill'); mūtārī is a passive infinitive

items.q: Quāle est cōnsilium Daedalī?
items.en: What is Daedalus' plan like?
items.hint: a predicate adjective agreeing with the neuter cōnsilium

items.q: Quid ad hoc opus necessārium est?
items.en: What is necessary for this work?
items.hint: three things listed in the accusative as objects of habeō

items.q: Cui Daedalus ālās ingentēs cōnfēcit?
items.en: For whom did Daedalus make huge wings?
items.hint: a dative of the person something is made for

items.q: Estne ars volandī difficilis?
items.en: Is the art of flying difficult?
items.hint: a yes/no question; the sentence answers with haud ('not at all'); volandī is a genitive gerund

items.q: Quis fugam Daedalī et Icarī animadvertit?
items.en: Who noticed the flight of Daedalus and Icarus?
items.hint: the nominative after nisi ('no one … except …')

items.q: Quālēs esse videntur illae īnsulae?
items.en: What do those islands seem to be like?
items.hint: a nominative plural adjective, the predicate after videntur esse

items.q: Utrum Peloponnēsus īnsula est an paenīnsula?
items.en: Is the Peloponnese an island or a peninsula?
items.hint: utrum … an offers two options; answer with the nominative predicate

items.q: Quid vocātur terra angusta quae Peloponnēsum cum Graeciā coniungit?
items.en: What is the narrow strip of land called that joins the Peloponnese to Greece?
items.hint: the nominative predicate with vocātur

items.q: Ubi sita est Corinthus?
items.en: Where is Corinth situated?
items.hint: prope + accusative

items.q: Cūr Icarus in summum caelum ascendit?
items.en: Why did Icarus climb into the highest sky?
items.hint: cupidus + a gerund in the genitive that takes its own object (sōlem … aspiciendī)

items.q: Quid ignis sōlis propinquī fēcit?
items.en: What did the fire of the nearby sun do?
items.hint: two perfect verbs, each with an accusative object

items.q: Quō puer territus cecidit?
items.en: Where did the terrified boy fall?
items.hint: in + accusative for place to which

items.q: Unde fīlius Sōlis cecidit?
items.en: From where did the son of the Sun fall?
items.hint: dē + ablative for place from which

items.q: Cūr fābula dē fīliō Daedalī nārrātur?
items.en: Why is the story of Daedalus' son told?
items.hint: the gerund in the genitive + causā ('for the sake of …')

items.q: Quis sibi in somnīs volāre vidētur?
items.en: Who seems to himself to be flying in his dreams?
items.hint: the nominative subject of vidētur (with sibi, 'to himself')
